Her original proposals, unveiled in November 2025, would double the qualifying period for settlement for most migrants from five to 10 years, and potentially triple it to 15 for care workers. Ms Mahmood is reportedly preparing to exempt existing social care workers from the lengthened timetable. The decision came after a backlash from a large number of Labour MPs who have suggested the reforms are unfair, with Ms Rayner previously describing the prospect of applying the rules retrospectively to migrants already in the UK as "un-British".
